newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Hostages released in Colombian prison drama.
newsitem.headline: Hostages released in Colombian prison drama.

text.p: Inmates released two more hostages being held at a prison in northern Colombia on Friday, a week after killing three guards and a policeman in a bloody takeover of the penitentiary, authorities said.

Spokesmen for the National Prisons Institute identified the freed hostages as Deneris Vega Acosta, a prison secretary, and Eduardo Avila, a construction engineer who was visiting the compound when it was taken over by rebellious inmates on April 3.
Eleven other hostages are still being held inside the prison in Valledupar, capital of northern Cesar province, by a group of about 10 heavily armed inmates, authorities said.

Jose Noe Rios, Colombia's deputy labour minister and chief negotiator with the rebellious prisoners, heralded Friday's release as a clear sign they were interested in restarting face-to-face talks that broke off during a tense standoff on Wednesday.
"It shows the goodwill of the rioters," he told local radio. "They're willing to make an effort to get back to the bargining table."
Three other hostages were freed on Monday, but tempers flared on Wednesday when authorities discovered a tunnel the inmates were apparently planning to use in a mass escape attempt.

Leaders of the takeover of the prison in Valledupar, an ageing facility housing more than 580 people but built to hold no more than 150, initially demanded helicopters and bullet-proof vests for a ride to freedom and possible exile in Cuba.

They have alternately demanded freedom for a select group of prisoners, improved living conditions including an end to chronic overcrowding, and a special judge to review their sentences on a case-by-case basis.
Most leaders of the uprising are in prison for murder or rebellion -- belonging to one of Colombia's leftist guerrilla groups. But former hostages say they were well-treated nonetheless.
"The treatment was very good, they treated us very well," said Vega Acosta. "I hope there can be a peaceful solution of this as soon as possible," she added of the eight-day-old prison standoff.
